name: ShiftERP
title: A multi-tenant SaaS ERP where every company runs on its own database
client: ShiftERP · SaaS ERP for co-packers and contract manufacturers
role: Full-stack developer: database-per-tenant architecture, super-admin tenant provisioning, subscription-gated modules, the report export layer and AWS deployment
summary: ShiftERP is a SaaS ERP for co-packers and supply-chain teams. Each company runs on its own isolated database, provisioned by a super admin and gated by its subscription, to manage customers, inventory, scheduling, accounting, supply chain and reporting.

metrics.label: report types in the report generator
output formats per report: screen, Excel, PDF

problem: Operations staff run reports such as inventory by lot, picking fees, cold-storage revenue, production by line and payroll export, then hand them to accounting or customers.
The report generator returned rows with nested objects and arrays. Exported as-is, those cells came out as raw JSON or blanks, and default column widths made long description columns unreadable.

constraints.label: Many shapes
constraints.text: Each of the 28 report types returns its own headers and rows, so export logic couldn't assume a fixed schema.

constraints.label: Tenant-scoped
constraints.text: Reports run inside the tenant resolved from the logged-in user, against that company's own database.

constraints.label: Existing controller
constraints.text: The work had to fit an established controller without changing what the report endpoints return.

architecture.caption: A super admin provisions a company and its database; its subscription opens modules, and every report can leave the app as a styled spreadsheet or a print-ready PDF.

sections.heading: Database per tenant
paras: Each company gets its own database through stancl/tenancy. Central migrations hold provisioning, billing and subscriptions; 105 tenant migrations and 74 tenant models hold the company's operational data. Middleware initialises the tenant from the signed-in user, so every query runs against that company's database and nothing else.

A super admin provisions new companies, creating the tenant database and its first admin, and the subscription decides which of the 6 modules a company can open: Customer Management, Inventory, Smart Scheduling, Accounting, Supply Chain and Reporting. The platform runs on AWS for every live tenant.

sections.heading: Export formatting that survives any report shape
paras: The Excel export picks column widths from the heading (wide for descriptions and product lists, narrower for names, ids, dates and amounts), centres and wraps every cell and styles a taller bold header row.

A recursive formatter decodes JSON strings, collapses id/name pairs to the name, joins scalar lists and drops internal ids. The PDF export reuses the same formatter and renders landscape A4 with dompdf.

challenges.title: Nested data in flat exports
challenges.text: Rows with nested arrays and objects rendered as raw data or empty cells. Recursive formatting now turns them into readable text and drops internal fields.

challenges.title: Unreadable default spreadsheets
challenges.text: Exports used uniform narrow columns with no wrapping. Heading-based widths, wrapping, alignment and a styled header made long descriptions readable.

challenges.title: No print-ready format
challenges.text: Reports could only be viewed in the app or exported to a spreadsheet. A dompdf template now gives every report type a landscape PDF through the same formatting path.

outcome: Companies are provisioned with their own database from the super-admin panel, open the modules their plan includes, and export all 28 report types as styled Excel or landscape PDF through one export path.
